sources.entry: Show Desktop - Hides every window with one click or a shortcut to show the Desktop, then brings them all back exactly as they were.

summary.one_liner: Show Desktop is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that hides every window with one click or a shortcut (default ⌃⇧D) and restores them exactly as they were.
summary.what_it_does: Show Desktop hides all open windows when you click its menu bar icon or press its keyboard shortcut (⌃⇧D by default, changeable to any combination or a single function key). A second click restores only the apps that were open, in the same order, with the previously used app in front. Apps already hidden before the first click stay hidden. Open Finder windows are minimized and restored too, which can be turned off. Apps are hidden the same way as ⌘H, so nothing is closed or quit. The README says the app has no internet access, enforced by the macOS App Sandbox, and needs no Accessibility or Screen Recording permission. Its only saved data is the shortcut choice and the Finder setting.
use_cases: Clear the Desktop to grab a file buried under windows
Hide all windows with one keystroke and restore them later
Get a Windows+D style show-desktop on a Mac
Quickly tidy the screen during a presentation or screen share
Hide Finder windows along with other apps
how_to_run: Download Show-Desktop.zip from the project's releases and unzip it
Move Show Desktop to the Applications folder and open it
Click the menu bar icon or press ⌃⇧D to show the Desktop
Build from source: git clone the repository and cd into show-desktop
notable: Restores windows in their original order with the previously focused app on top
Works without Accessibility, Input Monitoring or Screen Recording permissions
Enforced no-network sandbox, checked by CI on every build
Customizable global shortcut, including a single function key like F13
Runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs
caveats: Not notarized, so macOS shows a malware warning on first open; the README says the developer has not paid Apple's $99 yearly fee
Building from source requires Swift 6 (Xcode 16 or Command Line Tools)
Finder minimizing needs a macOS permission prompt; declining it leaves Finder windows unminimized
Shortcut conflicts with other apps may not be reported by macOS
